title: Coherent finite exceptional system of integral dual-pullback-dual
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site of a scheme $W$ put $B_{n,W}=(A_n)_W$ and $R_W=\lim_nB_{n,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use ordinary derived categories of module sheaves and the Roos-complete constructible category $D^b_c(W,R)$, whose finite reductions are constructible with a common bounded cohomological support [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-derived-complete]. Write $P_n=P\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{n,W}$ [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Use the strict semilinear coefficient-system category $\mathscr S_W$, the adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, its actual unit $u$ and counit $e$, and the mapping systems $\mathcal H_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; here $\mathcal R_WP=(P_n)_n$ with its coherent quotient maps and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix a compactification $f=pj$, with $j$ open and $p$ proper [def-nagata-compactification]. Use the functorial normalized finite-operation realizations $\mathcal F_f,\mathcal E_f$, the dualizing systems $\Omega_W$ and system duals $\mathcal D_W=\mathcal I_W(-,\Omega_W)$ of [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization].

For $W=X,Y$ put $\omega_{W,R}=\mathcal L_W\Omega_W$ with its specified reductions [prop-coef-integral-dualizing], and $D_{W,R}P=R\mathcal Hom_{R_W}(P,\omega_{W,R})$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $\theta:\mathcal E_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal D_Xf^*\mathcal D_Y$ for the specified system dual-formula comparison, where $f^*$ on systems is finite derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For every $L\in D^b_c(Y,R)$ put $M=D_{Y,R}L$, $F=f^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M=\mathcal L_X f^*\mathcal R_YM$ [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and $H=D_{X,R}F$.

The objects $M,F,H$ belong to their integral constructible categories. The systems $\mathcal R_WP$ for integral constructible $P$, $f^*\mathcal R_YM$, and $\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_YL$ are normalized. The evaluation-defined maps $\beta$ of the system calculus, composed with the dualizing counit $\mathcal R_W\omega_{W,R}\to\Omega_W$, give natural system isomorphisms
$$v_{W,P}:\mathcal R_WD_{W,R}P\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal D_W\mathcal R_WP.$$
The actual counit $e:\mathcal R_XF\to f^*\mathcal R_YM$ is a natural system isomorphism; its evaluations are the canonical completed-pullback comparisons, adjoint to the finite projections. Define
$$q_L=f^*(v_{Y,L})\circ e,\qquad b_L=\theta_{\mathcal R_YL}^{-1}\circ\mathcal D_X(q_L^{-1})\circ v_{X,F}.$$
Then $b_L:\mathcal R_XH\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal E_f\mathcal R_YL$ is a specified natural isomorphism in $D(\mathscr S_X)$; its evaluations are the canonical finite dual-formula maps, including both the completed-pullback and dualizing coefficient identifications. For integers $a\le b$, if every $L_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, and $d_X,d_Y\ge0$ are integer Krull-dimension bounds for $X,Y$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], every reduction of $H$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-2d_X,b+2d_Y]$. These statements specify the comparison at system level; no integral exceptional adjunction is asserted.

proof.text: For an integral constructible P, integral_residue_tor supplies a common finite Tor interval for its reductions. Transport the finite constructibility and Tor assertions through S.reductionEvaluation, and use S.reduction_normalized. This proves that S.reduction(P) lies in the normalized finite-Tor domain on X and Y.

Apply integralSystemDualityCompatibility on X and Y to the specified DualizingOperations. This gives constructibility of the integral dual M, invertibility of the actual dualComparison at every constructible input, and the single-dual uniform Tor bounds.

Apply completedSystemPullbackPreservation to M. Its actual total limit is exactly firstDualPullback, so F is constructible and the pulled-back reduction system is normalized. The preservation statement from step 2 on X then makes H constructible.

The prime ell is a unit on each scheme by its structure map to Spec D.k. Apply purNormalizedReconstruction to the pulled-back normalized system and to both normalized dualizing systems. This proves invertibility of the specific completed-pullback and dualizing counits. Naturality of dualComparison follows from reduction_compatible.naturality and bifunctoriality of system internal Hom. Its finite evaluation follows from fiber_naturality followed by beta_evaluation.

Define q using NatIso.ofComponents applied to qMap. Each component is invertible as the actual counit followed by pullback of the invertible dualComparison. Counit naturality followed by dualComparison naturality proves its naturality; its component equation is reflexivity.

Define b by NatIso.ofComponents: v at F, then system dual applied to q inverse, then theta inverse. Each factor is an isomorphism. Naturality of v, the opposite of q inverse naturality, and theta inverse naturality prove the required square. Its component equation is reflexivity.

Solve theta.finiteFormula for evaluation of theta inverse by cancelling evaluation of theta and the finite dual-formula isomorphism. Apply fiber_naturality to q inverse, and combine internal-Hom maps with map_comp. The first coefficient factor is the composite called finiteInverseQ, with the specified finite dualizing and pullback evaluations. This proves finite_component for the actual system comparison.

If L has Tor interval [a,b], the single-dual bound on Y gives [-b-2dY,-a]. The completed-pullback lemma preserves this interval for F. Apply the single-dual bound on X to F; a<=b and dY>=0 give the required ordered input interval. The output endpoints simplify to [a-2dX,b+2dY].

proof_origin.place: Integral dual preservation and reduction comparison, together with Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5); actual system-isomorphism assembly follows the original parent steps 4--8.
